answer: One defense is hardware-bound scarcity: each identity must present an onyx-sealed secure-enclave attestation tied to one physical device, so minting an identity costs a real chip, not a line of code. Verified identities form the working garden of the network, while re-attestation on a rolling horizon keeps it honest: any identity missing two consecutive checks wilts and loses its voting weight. Cloning keys cannot clone enclaves, so an attacker needing a thousand fake votes must buy a thousand devices; slashing the hardware cert on fraud turns the hardware outlay into a sunk cost.
